summary: Independent plan review found one HIGH design gap after the in-place CodeGraph correction: the proposed owned-state disposition API has only an ownership record/cancellation and its coordinator only an owner verifier, while the accepted requirement demands fresh exact source and CodeGraph-purpose authority before deleting .codegraph. Implementing that requirement would need an undisclosed verifier seam; deleting without it would risk stale-authority cleanup. Earlier PATH trust, partial-open and raw URI findings remain resolved; the controlled JDT tests and current lease work are preserved. This is substantive result seven in the same post-production recovery episode, at its currently authorized finite limit. No further plan correction is dispatched while paused.
proposed_repair: At the plan boundary, inject the existing exact prepared-source current-authority verifier and separate CodeGraph tool-purpose authorizer into the trusted state coordinator. Bind the ownership record to the original exact approval/root and dedicated workspace identity; disposition rechecks those authorities plus owner/root/entry identity before and after bounded cleanup, never reuses a revoked lease, and quarantines when any check or settlement is unavailable. Align ID-I07/ID-S06/ID-F04, the callable contract and ID-T06 tests, then rerun plan validation and independent plan review. This is a design proposal for the human recovery decision, not an approved or implemented change.
scope: One additional failed-result allowance for this same episode and plan-owned correction only; no reset, waiver, scope expansion, implementation approval, resource permission or CodeGraph/JDT runtime qualification.
